title: Smoked Salmon Pizzas with Dill Soured Cream and Red Onion
changes_from_base: Four small bases are baked with just olive oil and red onion, then spread with dill soured cream and topped with smoked salmon instead of tomato sauce and mozzarella; the optional caviar in the original is left out.
summary: Thin, crisp bases baked with olive oil and red onion, then spread with cool dill soured cream and topped with smoked salmon.
equipment: pizza peel or flat baking sheet

ingredients.item: pizza dough, shop-bought or homemade, at room temperature

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Set the oven to 260 °C with a pizza stone inside; allow 30 minutes for the stone to reach temperature.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Cut the 100 g smoked salmon into 5 cm squares and keep chilled until needed.

steps.title: Divide and shape
steps.text: Cut the 450 g dough into 4 equal pieces; roll or stretch each to a 20 cm circle and place either on a floured peel (if using a stone) or on oiled, floured baking trays.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Brush each base with a quarter of the 60 ml oil, stopping about 2.5 cm from the edge, then scatter the ½ thinly sliced red onion evenly.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake for 8 to 12 minutes until the crust is golden and firm.

steps.title: Meanwhile
steps.text: Stir the 4 tbsp finely chopped fresh dill into 80 g soured cream or crème fraîche, season with ¼ tsp ground black pepper.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Place each warm base on a warm serving plate, spread the dill cream across the surface, arrange the cold salmon squares on top, garnish each with a small dill sprig and serve immediately.

tips: Chill the salmon until the very last moment so it doesn't warm up too much from contact with the hot base
Serve immediately after topping so the creamy layer stays cool and the crust doesn't lose its crispness
safety: Cold-smoked salmon is not cooked: anyone pregnant or vulnerable should use hot-smoked salmon instead.
storage: Best eaten straight away; keep the salmon chilled until serving and eat any leftovers within 1 day. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
